newsitem.title: LEBANON: Japan Red Army members request retrial in Lebanon.
newsitem.headline: Japan Red Army members request retrial in Lebanon.

text.p: Five Japanese Red Army guerrillas sentenced to jail in Lebanon last month have appealed for a retrial, judicial sources said on Wednesday.
The sources said the lawyer for the four men and one woman made the appeal on Tuesday citing violations in the sentence.
The Red Army members were sentenced to three years each in jail on July 31 on charges relating to their illegal stay in the country.
Defence lawyer Beshara Abu Saad said the prisoners were not given a fair translation of the indictment and complained of nine other violations in his appeal for a retrial.

The guerrillas included Kozo Okamoto, who joined two comrades in a 1972 machinegun and grenade attack inside Tel Aviv's Lod airport in which 26 people died, including his two companions. He was captured but released later by Israel in a 1985 prisoner exchange.
Okamoto and Haruo Wako received only jail sentences. Masao Adachi, Mariko Yamamoto and Kazuo Tohira were also fined 600,000 Lebanese pounds ($390).
Defence lawyers said they would appeal the sentences at a higher court.
All five, who were arrested in Beirut last February, were convicted of entering the country with forged passports and forged visas.
The court rejected the guerrillas' defence that their crimes in Lebanon had been political. The defendants had asked for their release and the granting of political asylum.

The Red Army, founded in 1971, was allied to hardline anti-Israeli Palestinian factions. Many of its guerrillas stayed in Lebanon's Bekaa Valley which during the country's 1975-1990 civil war was a haven for guerrilla groups including Lebanese Moslems and Marxists, Palestinians, Kurds and the Red Army.
